title: Air India Suspends Delhi-Birmingham Nonstop Flights for Winter Season
excerpt: The three-times-weekly Delhi-Birmingham service is withdrawn from November 4, 2026 for winter 2026-27. Amritsar-Birmingham and four-daily Delhi-Heathrow remain the main Air India alternatives, and ticket holders should check rebooking and refund options now.
body:
• Air India's three-times-weekly Delhi-Birmingham nonstop is withdrawn from November 4, 2026 for the winter 2026-27 season; check any booking dated November 4 or later.
  • Amritsar-Birmingham continues at three flights a week in mid-November schedules, and Delhi-London Heathrow runs four times daily — the two main Air India alternatives.
  • If your flight is cancelled, contact Air India or your booking agent for rebooking or refund options, and manage the booking with your booking reference and last name on airindia.com.
  • No summer resumption date for Delhi-Birmingham has been confirmed in the schedule reporting; treat the route as suspended for the whole winter.

Air India has suspended its direct flights between Delhi and Birmingham for the winter 2026-27 season, removing the only nonstop link between India's capital and the West Midlands until at least the end of the winter schedule. The route operated three times a week and is withdrawn from November 4, 2026, according to timetable reporting by Live From A Lounge and Simple Flying, which both cite airline schedule data.

The cut is part of a wider European reshaping. On the same winter schedule, Air India has also withdrawn Delhi-Copenhagen from October 25, Amritsar-London Gatwick from October 25 and Delhi-Vienna from October 31. The reporting attributes the adjustments to higher aviation fuel costs, airspace restrictions and longer flight times on long-haul routes, which raise operating costs and reduce aircraft utilisation. Simple Flying, citing Cirium schedule data, puts Air India's European seat capacity between November 2026 and March 2027 at about 12% below the same period a year earlier.

What exactly is suspended

The suspended service is Delhi Indira Gandhi International Airport (DEL) to Birmingham Airport (BHX), three flights a week, effective November 4, 2026. Birmingham is not a small market for India travel: about 207,300 two-way passengers travelled between Birmingham and India during 2025, according to figures reported by Live From A Lounge, with Delhi accounting for about 53,600 of them. Air India had planned roughly 91,100 two-way seats across its Delhi-Birmingham and Amritsar-Birmingham services for this winter, a planned increase of 33.6% over the previous winter that will now not operate as filed on the Delhi route.

One distinction matters. Early schedule reporting suggested the three-times-weekly Amritsar-Birmingham service might also pause, but Simple Flying's mid-November network table still lists Amritsar-Birmingham at three flights a week. Travellers should still verify their specific dates, but on current schedules the Amritsar route is operating while the Delhi route is not.

Your alternatives from the Midlands

The most direct Air India alternative is Amritsar-Birmingham, still scheduled three times weekly, which suits travellers whose Indian journey can start or end in Punjab. The larger alternative is London Heathrow: Air India's Delhi-London Heathrow service runs four times daily in the mid-November schedule, with onward rail connections from London to Birmingham. Travellers can compare and book alternatives on Air India's official booking pages, which set out how website, app and agent bookings work.

One-stop itineraries through European or Gulf hubs are the other option, and they are also the fallback for the other suspended routes. What has changed is convenience, not connectivity: Birmingham passengers lose the nonstop and take on either a surface leg from Heathrow, a different Indian departure city, or a connection.

If you already hold a ticket

Live From A Lounge advises passengers booked to Birmingham, Vienna, Copenhagen or London Gatwick around the end of October and the start of November to check reservations carefully, and says passengers whose flights are cancelled should contact Air India or their booking agent to understand the available alternatives and the applicable rebooking or refund arrangements. Passengers with connecting itineraries should also confirm that a change to one flight does not break the rest of the journey.

On Air India's side, bookings can be retrieved and modified through Manage Booking on airindia.com or the app by entering the booking reference and the passenger's last name — no account login is required, according to the airline's FAQ. Full details of the winter changes and the remaining network are in the reporting from Live From A Lounge and Simple Flying.

Whether the Delhi-Birmingham nonstop returns for summer 2027 has not been confirmed in the reporting. Seasonal suspensions are not necessarily permanent cancellations, and Air India is simultaneously adding capacity elsewhere — Delhi-Sydney rises from seven to 11 flights a week, and a four-times-weekly Delhi-Osaka service is planned for February 2027. For this winter, however, Midlands travellers should plan on the assumption that the nonstop is gone.
